title: Space Fractional Dispersion and Time Fractional Multistage Deposition in Porous Media
content: Nonlocal spreading and history-dependent deposition jointly influence particle transport through porous media. We formulate and numerically solve a suspension-filtration model that combines one-sided Caputo spatial dispersion with time-fractional multistage deposition kinetics. A piecewise kinetic law describes initial loading, attachment–detachment, and a capacity threshold. We use implicit finite differences for transport and product integration for the temporal memory term. The simulations examine the effects of fractional orders on concentration profiles, deposition histories, outlet concentrations, and integrated retained mass. In the investigated cases, decreasing the deposition order reduces both near-inlet deposition and the final outlet concentration. The effects of spatial order depend on observation time, location, and kinetic order, producing changes in penetration and deposit distribution. Replacing the fractional deposit term in the suspension balance with an ordinary derivative substantially increases the predicted outlet concentration in the tested cases. Operator tests, residual checks, and separate spatial and temporal refinement assess numerical consistency and reveal greater outlet sensitivity to spatial resolution. These findings demonstrate that fractional-order effects must be interpreted together with the balance formulation and the distinction between physical deposition and history-dependent storage.
